evidence: The workbook Quality Checks!D48 and frozen skill check 47 require the shared model/agent, CLI/browser and shared-tool pins; the older Internal Quality Checks!D48 temperature/prompt-version/network wording is superseded by the explicit current profile. Frozen task/task.toml:30-38 exactly matches the frozen template verifier.env: claude-code, z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx, OpenRouter URL and credential templates, with public verifier network. Every parsed judge.toml uses the claude-code fallback and the installed playwright-mcp command with /usr/local/bin/chromium; no dimension overrides the model. Frozen task/tests/Dockerfile:16-21 pins Claude Code 2.1.281, Codex 0.151.0 and Playwright MCP 0.0.79; :31 pins harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7; :33-38 installs the browser using that pinned MCP package's own Playwright CLI. The fresh row47-pin-probe executed docker run --pull never --rm --name cw-row47-tooling-pin --network none -i against image sha256:46fefc505dbcabf0d6cb4e54fea8f0880acde2f7896587750af967427598977d. All four version commands exited 0: Claude Code 2.1.281, Codex 0.151.0, MCP 0.0.79 and Chrome 152.0.7977.8. Installed MCP package.json pins both playwright and playwright-core exactly to 1.63.0-alpha-2026-08-05; that core's browsers.json fixes Chromium revision 1237 / 152.0.7977.8. The task and frozen-template tests/Dockerfile, test.sh, score.py and restart_mcp.py are byte-identical. SHA256 values respectively are 72998ab8ef0e4225e63b88fccdb754943c54022e25da355035efe7f759a55fdd, bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa, 13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e and 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5. The fresh image probe independently found those same two shared-tool hashes baked in /tests/tools. No graded calendar/date-dependent rule or seeded date exists in this playground. Public behaviour.md:9,19,21 asks for five-second run budgets, elapsed duration and debouncing. Functional prompt.md:15,113,257-267,381-398,465-475 measures elapsed behavior from actual browser actions with explicit margins, timed actions in one browser call, observed debounce windows and successful controls. Date.now at prompt.md:36 only creates a unique intercepted-network nonce; test.sh:178 uses date only in a diagnostic log. Neither changes a graded calendar figure. A frozen business clock is consequently inapplicable here; freezing timer progress would obstruct the requested real timer behavior. Adversarial source challenges: an app that always displays a fixed duration cannot satisfy S16 (:387 requires the short/delayed executions to differ); an app resetting its budget for every callback exposes the forbidden six-second completion in S36 (:473-474). A conforming app using rounded seconds, a different valid debounce interval, provisional hidden previews, or allowed external browser assets is explicitly accepted (:15,387-398 and app_context.md:18). These are source/protocol challenges, not executed mutant apps or measured judge outcomes. Verified pre-existing raw smoke hashes: tooling-observations.json ae762aea9e1256e9e48c8dccbe989e6ce2821e6bd1e4fffd90151fbf3c29d562 and observations.json f482247670bfc5de13dfb47a8f25fb649c7ba09bad67c82a381789b4950ad98c match the current index; their own scope explicitly excludes configured grading.
